content: 1. Anhydrous sodium citrate reduces the levels of levofloxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction is relevant only when both agents are administered orally. Caution and monitoring are advised. Products containing multivalent cations can decrease the bioavailability of quinolones; therefore, quinolones should be administered at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after magnesium-containing products. Alternatives should be considered if available. 2. Both levofloxacin and trimethoprim prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. Levofloxacin and trimipramine both increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 4. Triptorelin increases the toxicity of levofloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval, which raises the risk of torsades de pointes. Caution and monitoring are advised. 5. Tropisetron and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 6. Valbenazine and levofloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 7. Levofloxacin and venlafaxine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 8. Levofloxacin enhances the effects of vildagliptin through pharmacodynamic synergy. Caution and monitoring are advised. 9. Quinolone antibiotics, including levofloxacin, may cause hyperglycemia or hypoglycemia. Gatifloxacin is most likely to cause dysglycemia, while moxifloxacin is least likely. 10. Voclosporin and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 11. Voriconazole and levofloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 12. Vorinostat and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 13. Levofloxacin increases the effects of warfarin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 14. Zinc reduces the levels or effects of levofloxacin by binding cations in the gastrointestinal tract. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Oral levofloxacin should be administered 2 hours before or after products containing polyvalent cations. 15. Levofloxacin and ziprasidone both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 16. Levofloxacin and aceclofenac may increase the risk of central nervous system (CNS) stimulation or seizures. This is due to the displacement of GABA from its receptors in the brain. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 17. Levofloxacin and acemetacin may increase the risk of CNS stimulation or seizures through GABA receptor displacement. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 18. Levofloxacin increases the levels of alprazolam by reducing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 19. Azithromycin and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 20. Levofloxacin reduces the levels or effects of balsalazide by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 21. Levofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of biotin by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 22. Levofloxacin increases the levels of chlordiazepoxide by reducing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 23. Levofloxacin and choline magnesium trisalicylate may increase the risk of CNS stimulation or seizures through GABA receptor displacement. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 24. Levofloxacin increases the levels of clonazepam by reducing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 25. Levofloxacin increases the levels of clorazepate by reducing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 26. Levofloxacin increases the levels of estazolam by reducing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 27. Levofloxacin and fenbufen may increase the risk of CNS stimulation or seizures through GABA receptor displacement. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 28. Levofloxacin increases the levels of flurazepam by reducing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 29. Foscarnet and levofloxacin may increase the risk of tonic-clonic seizures through an unknown mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 30. Levofloxacin increases the levels of green tea by reducing its elimination. Some quinolones can inhibit the hepatic clearance of caffeine. Caution is advised. 31. Levofloxacin and isotretinoin may increase the risk of phototoxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 32. Itraconazole and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 33. Levofloxacin increases the levels of loprazolam by reducing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 34. Levofloxacin increases the levels of lorazepam by reducing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 35. Levofloxacin increases the levels of lormetazepam by reducing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 36. Levofloxacin and lornoxicam may increase the risk of CNS stimulation or seizures through GABA receptor displacement. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 37. Levofloxacin increases the levels of midazolam by reducing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 38. Levofloxacin increases the levels of oxazepam by reducing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 39. Levofloxacin reduces the levels or effects of pantothenic acid by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 40. Levofloxacin and parecoxib may increase the risk of CNS stimulation or seizures through GABA receptor displacement. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 41. Levofloxacin and pazopanib both prolong the QTc interval. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 42. Levofloxacin reduces the levels or effects of pyridoxine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 43. Levofloxacin increases the levels of quazepam by reducing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 44. Quercetin reduces the effects of levofloxacin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 45. Levofloxacin and salicylates (non-ASA) may increase the risk of CNS stimulation or seizures through GABA receptor displacement. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 46. Levofloxacin increases the levels of temazepam by reducing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 47. Levofloxacin reduces the levels or effects of thiamine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 48. Levofloxacin and tolfenamic acid may increase the risk of CNS stimulation or seizures through GABA receptor displacement. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 49. Levofloxacin increases the levels of triazolam by reducing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 50. Levofloxacin enhances the effects of acarbose through pharmacodynamic synergy. Caution and monitoring are advised.
